title: Shortest Subarray to be Removed to Make Array Sorted
summary: Given an integer array, identify the shortest contiguous subarray that can be removed to ensure the remaining elements are in non-decreasing order.
statement: Given an integer array, identify the shortest contiguous subarray that can be removed to ensure the remaining elements are in non-decreasing order. Return the length of this subarray.
constraints: Remove one contiguous subarray, possibly empty.
Minimize its length so the remaining values are non-decreasing.
reference_solution:
def shortest_sorted_removal(arr):
 n=len(arr);right=n-1
 while right and arr[right-1]<=arr[right]:right-=1
 if right==0:return 0
 answer=right;left=0
 while left==0 or arr[left-1]<=arr[left]:
  while right<n and arr[right]<arr[left]:right+=1
  answer=min(answer,right-left-1);left+=1
  if left==n:break
 return answer

hints: Find the longest non-decreasing suffix and use removing its prefix as an initial answer.
Advance through the non-decreasing prefix while moving the suffix pointer until its first value can follow the current prefix value.
The gap between those pointers is the removal length.
Every valid remainder consists of a prefix joined to a suffix, and the monotone pointer checks each possible prefix end optimally.
